Which remediation option on the Protect tab should you use?
choices: Restrict all items
Restrict access by label
Create an auto-labeling policy
Create retention policies
explanation: The Protect tab of a data risk assessment offers Restrict access by label (DLP for Copilot), Restrict all items (SharePoint Restricted Content Discovery), auto-labeling and retention policies. Restricted Content Discovery excludes a whole site from Copilot without changing permissions, which suits unlabeled content.
rationale: Correct: Restrict all items uses SharePoint Restricted Content Discovery to exclude the listed site from Microsoft 365 Copilot, and it does not change who can access the site, so permissions stay as they are.

Incorrect: Restrict access by label creates a DLP policy that keeps labeled items out of Copilot. The files are unlabeled, so nothing would be excluded. Use it when sensitive content already has labels.
Incorrect: an auto-labeling policy labels sensitive files over time, but labeling alone does not stop Copilot, and simulation must run first. Use it to fix unlabeled sensitive data at scale.
Incorrect: retention policies from the Protect tab delete content that has not been accessed for years. They do not stop Copilot from using current files. Use them to remove stale data.

stem:
Relecloud must find individual files in five SharePoint sites that have sharing links for external or anonymous users, and remove those links from Data Security Posture Management (DSPM). The default data risk assessment shows only site-level results.

What should you do?
choices: Run a custom item-level assessment that uses a registered Entra app
Run a custom assessment for the five sites at the site level
Run a custom item-level assessment for the users' OneDrive accounts
Run an on-demand classification scan from the Identify tab
explanation: In DSPM and DSPM for AI (classic), custom data risk assessments can scan at item level for SharePoint sites (up to 10) after a one-time authentication with a registered Microsoft Entra app that has Microsoft Graph application permissions. Item-level results list potentially overshared items with actions such as Remove sharing link.
rationale: Correct: an item-level custom assessment, authenticated with a registered Entra app, lists potentially overshared items in up to 10 SharePoint sites and offers Remove sharing link as a remediation action.
Incorrect: a site-level custom assessment has the same granularity as the default one and gives no per-file remediation. Use it to check sites or users that the default assessment does not cover.
Incorrect: OneDrive currently is not supported for item-level scanning, and the files are in SharePoint sites. Use a OneDrive assessment only for site-level insights.
Incorrect: an on-demand classification scan detects sensitive information types in items that were not scanned. It does not list sharing links or remove them. Use it when files are unclassified.

stem:
Adatum Corporation uses the current version of Microsoft Purview Data Security Posture Management. The security team needs an inventory of all AI apps and agents with activity in the last 30 days, including Microsoft Agent 365 agents, and how many are high risk.

Which page should you use?
choices: AI observability
Discover > Apps and agents
Asset explorer
Reports
explanation: In the current DSPM, AI observability inventories AI apps and agents, including Microsoft Agent 365, with risk and sensitive-interaction counts. Discover > Apps and agents shows a dashboard of AI apps and agents but does not include Agent 365.
rationale: Correct: AI observability lists all AI apps and agents with activity in the last 30 days, including Agent 365, with how many are high risk and how many had sensitive interactions.
Incorrect: Apps and agents shows AI apps and their agents and details for the top 20 recently used agents, but Learn states it does not include Agent 365. Use it for agent details outside Agent 365.
Incorrect: Asset explorer gives a unified view of labeled and classified data by workload and location. It is a data inventory, not an AI app inventory.
Incorrect: Reports track sensitive data usage, labeling, policy usage and risky behavior over time. They do not inventory each AI app and agent with its risk level.

stem:
Tailspin Toys wants Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) to scan individual files in three SharePoint sites for oversharing and to remove risky sharing links.

Which four actions should you perform in sequence? To answer, move the appropriate actions from the list of actions to the answer area and arrange them in the correct order.
choices: Register an app in the Microsoft Entra admin center for accounts in this organizational directory only.
Add Microsoft Graph application permissions such as Sites.ReadWrite.All and Files.ReadWrite.All, grant admin consent, and create a client secret.
Create a custom data risk assessment, select Item-level on the Scan level page, and select Authenticate.
Open the Potentially overshared items tab and select Remove sharing link for the items.
Enable Service principals can access read-only admin APIs in the Fabric admin portal.
Run an on-demand classification scan from the Identify tab of the default assessment.
explanation: Item-level scanning needs a one-time authentication with a registered Entra app: register it, add the Microsoft Graph application permissions with admin consent, create a client secret, and provide the app ID and secret when you create the item-level custom assessment. Results with remediation actions appear after the scan completes.
rationale: Step 1: item-level scanning authenticates with a registered Entra app, so the app must exist first. It uses the single-tenant account type.

Step 2: the app needs Microsoft Graph application permissions such as Sites.ReadWrite.All, Files.ReadWrite.All and SensitivityLabels.Read.All with admin consent, plus a client secret that you save now because it is shown only once.
Step 3: in DSPM > Discover > Data risk assessments, the custom assessment with Item-level scan level and Authenticate uses the app values to scan the selected SharePoint sites.
Step 4: after the scan is complete, the Potentially overshared items tab lists items with sharing links for external or anonymous users, and Remove sharing link remediates them.
Incorrect: the Fabric Admin API settings are part of the one-time setup for Fabric data risk assessments. SharePoint item-level scanning does not need them.
Incorrect: an on-demand classification scan finds sensitive information types in unscanned items. It is not required for item-level oversharing scans. Use it when data is not yet classified.

stem:
Lucerne Publishing uses Data Security Posture Management (DSPM). The company must first discover, in audit mode, when users paste or upload sensitive content to third-party AI sites in Edge, Chrome and Firefox. It must also give users with elevated risk a block with override when they paste sensitive information into those sites.

Which two one-click policies should you create? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.
choices: DSPM for AI: Detect sensitive info added to AI sites
DSPM for AI - Block sensitive info from AI sites
DSPM for AI - Capture interactions for enterprise AI apps
DSPM for AI - Protect sensitive data from Copilot processing
DSPM for AI - Unethical behavior in AI apps
explanation: DSPM (Tasks and actions > Remediation actions) and DSPM for AI (classic) create one-click policies in other Purview solutions. Discovery policies run in audit mode, and protection policies such as Block sensitive info from AI sites use Adaptive Protection to block risky users with override. Collection, Copilot DLP and communication compliance policies cover other scenarios.
rationale: Correct: this DLP policy discovers sensitive content pasted or uploaded to AI sites in Edge, Chrome and Firefox for all users in audit mode only, which meets the discovery requirement.

Correct: this DLP policy uses Adaptive Protection to give elevated-risk users a block with override when they paste or upload sensitive information to AI sites in Edge, Chrome and Firefox. It is created in test mode, so turn it on after you review the results.

Incorrect: this collection policy captures prompts and responses from enterprise AI apps such as ChatGPT Enterprise and Entra-registered or Foundry apps. It does not cover third-party consumer sites or block anything.

Incorrect: this DLP policy stops Microsoft 365 Copilot and agents from processing items with selected sensitivity labels. It does not act on third-party AI sites. Use it to protect labeled data from Copilot.
Incorrect: this communication compliance policy detects sensitive information and unethical behavior in prompts and responses for review. It does not block pastes. Use it for conduct monitoring.

stem:
You need to meet the requirement for User1 and the review of Copilot prompts and responses.

Which role should you assign to User1?
choices: Purview Data Security AI Content Viewer
Purview Data Security AI Viewer
Microsoft Purview Compliance Administrator
Microsoft Entra AI Administrator
explanation: Viewing the text of prompts and responses in AI interaction events of activity explorer is not included in the admin or view-only roles of DSPM for AI. It requires Content Explorer Content Viewer or the narrower Purview Data Security AI Content Viewer role, which is limited to AI interactions.
rationale: Correct: Data Security AI Content Viewer grants access to prompts and responses in AI interaction events only, so it is the narrowest role that adds what User1 lacks while keeping least privilege.
Incorrect: Data Security AI Viewer is a view-only role for DSPM for AI pages, similar to the Security Reader access User1 already has. It does not show prompt and response text.
Incorrect: the Compliance Administrator role group can create and edit in DSPM for AI, but the permissions table shows that it cannot view prompts and responses, and it is broader than needed.
Incorrect: the Entra AI Administrator role has view-only access in DSPM for AI and manages Copilot settings tenant-wide. It does not show prompt text and exceeds least privilege.
